title.narrative: Cambodia-Institutionalization of Project & Program Management Functions

description.narrative: The Grant would promote the establishment and utilization of the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) regular structures and staffing to identify, prepare, implement, monitor and evaluate development projects. This would be achieved through the integration of the PMUs into existing government structures and through the establishment of results-based M&E systems. PMUs. The IDF Grant would help the RGC implement the one action of the Harmonization/Alignment Action Plan which aims to integrate PMUs functions into standard government structures. This is consistent with the January 2004 CPPR's recommendation that donors and the government explore ways to streamline the use of PMUs. The main activities financed by the grant would consist of: i. undertaking a study tour to a neighboring country which have integrated project implementation functions successfully in order to share experience; ii. reviewing management and implementation arrangements of ODA-financed projects in most sectors and recommending changes to promote the utilization and development of efficient, transparent and accountable of existing normal administrative structures; iii. helping the government reach consensus around the recommended actions with the donors community through workshops and other consultative meetings; and iv. supporting the implementation of the strategy through provision of technical assistance, training and equipment. The expected outcome is strengthened internal capacity of selected line ministries to perform effectively project management functions in a manner that promote transparency and accountability. M&E This IDF Grant would help introduce results-based M&E systems that would help RGC decision makers assess whether and how goals are being achieved over time. The main activities will consist of: i. assessing the existing monitoring and evaluation systems of the government and concerned line ministries and identify capacity constraints; ii. providing concerned government staff knowledge and skills in logic models, evaluation criteria, key performance indicators, data collection and analysis, reporting and evaluations management; iii. helping establish sustainable results-based M&E systems; and iv. audit of the grant The expected outcome is increased transparency, accountability and effectiveness of the ODA-financed activities. The purpose of the Grant is to assist the Royal Government of Cambodia to establish and utilize its administrative structures and staff to identify, prepare, implement, monitor, and evaluate development projects. The activities for which the Grant is given are as follows: Part A: Integration of Project Management Units 1. Carrying out studies to learn from successful experiences in integrating project implementing functions. 2. Reviewing the management and implementation arrangements of projects financed by development agencies to promote the utilization and development of efficient, transparent and accountable administrative structures. 3. Carrying out workshops and consultative meetings with the donor community for the purposes of sharing experiences and knowledge and build concensus around a common strategy to integrate project implementation functions. 4. Designing and implementing a strategy to integrate project implementation functions. Part B: Monitoring and Evaluation 1. Assessing the current monitoring and evaluation systems of the government and ministries to identify knowledge, skills and institutional constraints. 2. Training government staff in evaluation criteria, key performance indicators, date collection and analysis, and reporting and evaluation management. 3. Establishing sustainable results-based monitoring and evaluation systems. 4. Audting the use of Grant funds.
